newsitem.title: UK: UK farm incomes up 65 pct in five years, down in 9.
newsitem.headline: UK farm incomes up 65 pct in five years, down in 9.

text.p: British farm incomes have risen by 65 per cent in real terms over the last five years, according to the Ministry of Agriculture.
Although there was a decline of 5.4 per cent in 1996, in real terms incomes remain higher than in 1994 and the preceding 10 years.
"Over the last few years we have seen a very considerable rise in farm incomes, farm minister Douglas Hogg said in a statement.
"The fall in 1996 follows a rise of over 75 per cent in Total Income From Farming in real terms over the four year period up to 1995," Hogg said.
But National Farmers Union president David Naish described the figures as "warning signals of a situation which could worsen significantly in the future."
In a statement, the NFU said the decline was mainly the result of lower cereal, potato and beef prices, combined with a sharp increase in the cost of inputs such as feed and fertilisers.

"If farm incomes come under further pressure I do believe the industry is amply justified in seeking further support in line with other (EU) member states, including to recognise the revaluation of the green pound," Naish said.

The revaluation of the so-called green rate, used to convert agricultural prices and subsidy levels set in Ecu into sterling, will further hit incomes. The NFU is seeking government compensation for the losses it causes.
